s1.publisher: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
s1.quote: The vessel lies between French Reef and Dixie Shoals surrounded by low-profile coral reef and sand in depths ranging from 25 to 45 feet. … The bow of the ship is the most-intact feature, forming a 25-foot vertical profile in the water column.

s2.quote: Resident schools of porkfish, goatfish and schoolmaster snapper are the iconic highlights.

highlights.text: Intact bow rising about 25 ft off the bottom
Resident porkfish, goatfish and schoolmaster snapper

summary.text: A freighter lost in 1942 and now a Florida Keys Shipwreck Trail dive off Key Largo, lying in 25-45 ft among low reef and sand. The bow is the most complete section, and schooling snapper and porkfish make it a popular, comfortable wreck dive.

s1.quote: Her top deck is about 60 feet (18 m) below the water's surface. … is as much as 135 feet (41 m) under water. … The depth of the wreck requires that divers have an advanced certification. … Silt can get kicked up and reduce visibility inside to almost zero, which can cause disorientation.

s2.quote: so immense that each dive is but a vignette of the whole. … overhead environment beyond ambient light

hazards.text: Silt-outs inside the hull cause disorientation

highlights.text: Huge wreck: one dive covers only a fraction of it

summary.text: A 510-ft Navy landing ship dock sunk off Key Largo as an artificial reef, with its top deck near 60 ft and hull to about 135 ft. Its sheer size rewards repeat dives, but depth and a silt-prone interior make it an advanced-diver wreck.

s1.quote: more protected than many other reefs, making it a fine option for choppy, windy days. … bright-purple fan corals swaying gently in the current

s2.quote: Grecian Rocks sits just south of the Christ of the Abyss statue, off the coast of Key Largo. … parts of the reef are exposed at high tide making it a popular snorkeling site

highlights.text: Purple fan corals swaying in the current

summary.text: A shallow patch reef off Key Largo beside the Christ of the Abyss site, whose crest breaks the surface at high tide. It is sheltered enough to dive or snorkel on breezy days and is rich in fan corals and reef fish.

s1.quote: 12-25 feet … Open Water … Any one of the 2 or 3 mooring balls features abundant colorful coral and tropical fish under it.

highlights.text: Coral mounds with abundant tropical fish

s1.quote: resting in eight-ten ft. of water, three-four ft. below the surface. … The preserve is open to the public year round, free of charge.

s2.quote: 8 to 10 feet (2.4 to 3 m) of water … Mooring balls … especially suited for snorkelers because of its depth … damselfish, sergeant majors, spiny lobster, bristle worms, angelfish and porcupinefish

access.value: Florida Underwater Archaeological Preserve; open year round, free of charge

highlights.text: Damselfish, sergeant majors, spiny lobster, angelfish

summary.text: The 1930 wreck of a former racing yacht sits on a shoal off Key Biscayne in only 8-10 ft of water, with just a few feet over the hull. A free state archaeological preserve with mooring balls, it suits snorkelers and relaxed shallow dives.

s1.quote: rests in only 25 feet of water … excellent for the beginner diver … a couple hundred feet off the Delray Beach Municipal Beach

s2.quote: located about 150 yards (140 m) offshore … is now a popular dive site

summary.text: The remains of a steamship wrecked in a 1903 hurricane lie just off Delray Beach's public beach in about 25 ft of water. The shallow depth and short distance from shore make it a popular first wreck for newer divers and snorkelers.

s1.quote: 90 feet under water, roughly 28 nautical miles off of Sanibel Island … 2 Moorings: Bow and Stern … Highest Relief: 60 Feet

s2.quote: 28 nautical miles off the coast of Captiva Island … the first dedicated veterans memorial military ship reef in the United States of America

highlights.text: Upright 165-ft cutter with smokestack and engine room

summary.text: A 165-ft Coast Guard cutter sunk in 2012 as a veterans memorial reef about 28 nautical miles offshore of southwest Florida. Resting upright in roughly 90 ft with bow and stern moorings, it is a boat-only wreck dive.

s1.quote: 40-60 feet; just east of Mar-A-Lago, Trump's seaside mansion, is a prolific reef less visited by divers, who enjoy the ledge relief and numerous fish.
Swarming with sponges, bright tropical fish and many sea creatures … inward and outward ledge drop … shallow and quiet dive site … recommended for intermediate divers

s2.quote: Dive sites such as Juno's Ledge and Flower Gardens offered up both the small stuff with numerous types of shrimp, crab and nudis to the big stuff with Goliath grouper, barracuda and sharks.

highlights.text: Sponges, tropical fish, Goliath grouper, barracuda

summary.text: A ledge reef a few miles off Palm Beach with an inside and outside drop, covered in sponges and busy with reef fish. Calm and fairly shallow, it ranges from small critters to grouper and barracuda and suits intermediate divers.

s1.quote: Dutch 164 foot long shipwreck that rests one mile north of the Jupiter Inlet … about 90 feet of water … compartments and the fascinating engine room

highlights.text: Compartments and engine room in a 164-ft steel hull

s1.quote: Those without at least a cavern certification at Orange Grove may only dive if an instructor is present. … your caver certification card on your vehicle dashboard while you are diving so that the rangers may check. … Scooters (DPVs) are not allowed in Peacock Springs

s2.quote: over 38,000 feet of passages … one of the longest underwater cave systems in the continental United States

access.value: State park; certification card displayed on dashboard; cavern/cave cert needed in cave systems; no scooters

hazards.text: Overhead cave passages require cave certification

summary.text: A Suwannee County state park holding one of the longest underwater cave networks in the continental U.S. Divers walk in from the car park, must show certification, and need cavern or cave training for most of the systems; scooters are banned.

s1.quote: 10 miles off the coast of Honeymoon Island State Park in the Gulf of Mexico … 36 to 40 ft (11 to 12 m) … average visibility of 31 to 35 ft (9.4 to 10.7 m) … by boat

highlights.text: Ring of 13 veteran statues around a central monument

s1.quote: The 407 ffw depth makes the cave system under Weeki Wachee springs the deepest known freshwater cave system in the United States. … the discharge level at Weeki Wachee spring dropped to a level that allowed for cave divers to gain effective entry into the cave system

access.value: Cave entry only practical when spring discharge is unusually low (as in 2007)

highlights.text: Deepest known freshwater cave system in the US

s2.quote: is a recreational dive site of the Florida Panhandle Shipwreck Trail

s1.quote: 70-foot-deep … offers many opportunities for swimming, snorkeling, and diving … the remains of the Civil War-era steamboat Madison, which was scuttled at the spring in 1863

highlights.text: Civil War steamboat Madison scuttled in 1863

summary.text: A 70-ft-deep spring on the Suwannee River whose main draw is the steamboat Madison, scuttled in 1863 to keep it from capture. Open for swimming, snorkeling and diving.

s1.quote: 10-15 ft. of water … 200 yards offshore … The preserve is open to the public year round, free of charge.

s2.quote: 10 to 15 feet (3 to 4.5 m) of water on the first offshore reef … 200 yards (180 m) offshore … sea urchins, sea cucumbers, flounder, wrasse and blue tang

access.value: Underwater archaeological preserve; free, open year round; no souvenir collecting

highlights.text: Sea urchins, flounder, wrasse and blue tang

summary.text: Florida's first underwater archaeological preserve: the scattered remains of a 1715 Spanish treasure fleet ship lie 200 yards off Fort Pierce in 10-15 ft of water. Shallow and free to visit, it is a good snorkel or easy dive.
